Astral Adventurer's Guide (Spelljammer: Adventures in Space)

summary.2e: The rainbow-colored, flammable medium that fills the space between the crystal spheres. Currents in it (the Flow) carry ships between spheres.
summary.5e: The silvery plane between the wildspace systems. A ship moves through it when its captain concentrates on a destination.

regions.name: The Known Spheres
regions.summary: A stable group of spheres around the triangle of Realmspace, Greyspace and Krynnspace, with Herospace, Greatspace, Darkspace, Faeriespace and Clusterspace. Some books use the name for the core three alone, or for all of known space.

regions.name: Arcane Inner Flow
regions.summary: A stable group of fewer than a dozen spheres near Realmspace, among them Refuge, Pirtelspace and Darnannonspace. Two-way currents join its neighbors.

regions.name: Vodoni Empire
regions.summary: Twelve spheres that Emperor Vulkaran the Dark rules from Vodonispace. Its currents reach Realmspace, Greyspace and Krynnspace.

spheres.name: Realmspace
spheres.summary: The crystal sphere around Toril's system. Glyphs hundreds of miles tall cover the inside of the shell, and the stars are openings to the quasi-elemental plane of Radiance.
facts: Glyphs and wards hundreds of miles tall line the inside. Reading one releases a spell at 100 times normal power.
About 3,200 open at any time. The Wanderers, a line of cursed souls who walk the inside of the shell, chant them open.

bodies.name: The Sun
bodies.summary: The primary of Realmspace, at the exact center of the sphere. Creatures from the elemental plane of Fire live on it, and they attack any ship that comes within ten million miles.
facts: Creatures from the elemental plane of Fire

bodies.name: The Sargassos
bodies.summary: Twelve magic-dead globes, each 100,000 miles across, on an orbit 40 million miles from the Sun. Helms and magic items stop inside them.
facts: Helms fade, then stop. The helmsman falls into spelljammer shock for four days.

bodies.name: Anadia
bodies.summary: The innermost planet, small and amber-green, cut by canyons larger than the Great Rift. Halflings live at both poles. The hot equator belongs to umber hulks and other Anadian beasts.
facts: Halflings at the poles, umber hulks at the equator
Once used as a debris storage area

bodies.name: Coliar
bodies.summary: A huge world of air. Floating islands of earth and water orbit its core, between 50 and 30,000 miles from the center. Avian humanoids and reptiles live on them.
facts: Floats about 100 miles above the core

bodies.name: Toril
bodies.summary: The third planet and the most populous world in Realmspace, with the widest variety of life. Selûne orbits it, and the Tears of Selûne trail behind the moon.
facts: Chunming in Shou Lung, and Calimport, where ships must land on the water away from the city

bodies.name: Selûne
bodies.summary: Toril's moon, 183,000 miles out. The same side always faces Toril. Its people worship Leira, and most of them are elves and humans.

bodies.name: Tears of Selûne
bodies.summary: A cluster of asteroids that trails behind Selûne on the same orbit, 183,000 miles from Toril. Elves and humans live here, with other spacefaring races.
facts: Elves and humans, with a smattering of other spacefaring races

bodies.name: Rock of Bral
bodies.summary: An asteroid in the Tears of Selûne and the site of the city of Bral, a port for spelljamming ships from many spheres.

sources.title: Faiths & Avatars (cited by the Forgotten Realms Wiki)

bodies.name: Karpri
bodies.summary: An ocean world. Pack ice hundreds of miles thick covers the poles, and mats of weed on the equator carry huge insects. Aquatic elves live in the seas.
facts: Aquatic elves, huge insects, arctic predators

bodies.name: Chandos
bodies.summary: A water world. Rocks pile up in its seas into islands that do not stay stable. The people descend from the crews of two spelljammers that crashed here long ago.

bodies.name: Glyth
bodies.summary: A harsh gray world with a ring and three moons. Mind flayers have held it for about a century, and most activity happens underground.
facts: Mind flayers and many humanoid races

bodies.name: Rings of Glyth
bodies.summary: A ring of small asteroids and ice balls around Glyth's equator. The mind flayers keep captive oortlings on it.

bodies.name: Haven
bodies.summary: A hollowed asteroid between the first and second rings of Glyth. Warring mind flayer factions treat it as neutral ground.
facts: Between Glyth's first and second rings

bodies.name: Mingabwe
bodies.summary: A bitterly cold moon of Glyth and a trading post for merchants who are not mind flayers.

bodies.name: Polluter
bodies.summary: A small, unmapped moon that orbits Mingabwe.

bodies.name: Garden
bodies.summary: Not one world but a chain of earth masses held together by one enormous plant, Yggdrasil's Child. It has twelve moons, and pirates have dens here.

bodies.name: H'Catha
bodies.summary: A flat disc of water 300 miles thick with one mountain, the Spindle, at its center. The Spindle always points at the Sun. Beholders hold the world.

bodies.name: Turnbetl
bodies.summary: The closer moon of H'Catha. Its atmosphere is made of highly unstable gases.

bodies.name: Lumbe
bodies.summary: The farthest moon of H'Catha: a metal cylinder 600 by 75 feet that tumbles like a baton. Behind two locked doors is an empty mage's laboratory.

bodies.name: Comet K'Thoutek
bodies.summary: A comet of iron and ice about 300 miles across. It travels at right angles to the planets' orbits and takes more than 237 years to go around the Sun. Toril's astrologers read great births in its appearances.
facts: Only within 200 million miles of the Sun

bodies.name: Skull of the Void
bodies.summary: A human skull of bone 12 miles high and 10 miles wide. It does not move and orbits nothing, about 50 million miles inside the shell. It repairs itself and makes its own air.
facts: Fixed, about 50 million miles from the shell

bodies.name: Caer Windlauer
bodies.summary: A castle with ten spires on 2,000 acres of land, sent into orbit around the Sun by a wish. Its orbit runs between Coliar's and Karpri's distances, at 45 degrees to Toril's.
facts: 100 to 300 million miles from the Sun, tilted 45 degrees
About 2,000 acres, with a pond and streams that flow in a circle

bodies.name: Galleon Nebula
bodies.summary: A nebula shaped like a multicolored galleon under sail, two million miles long and high. Through a spyglass its oars seem to row. Toril sees it mostly in autumn and early winter.
facts: 2 million miles long and high, over 100,000 miles wide

bodies.name: Color Spray Nebula
bodies.summary: A fan-shaped nebula that looks like a color spray spell, about two million miles long. Worshipers of Mystra take it as a sign of her favor. Toril sees it in spring and early summer.
facts: About 2 million miles long, 1 million wide at the open end

spheres.name: Greyspace
spheres.summary: The crystal sphere of the world of Oerth. Not charted on this map yet.

sources.title: Concordance of Arcane Space (cited by the Forgotten Realms Wiki)

spheres.name: Krynnspace
spheres.summary: The crystal sphere of the world of Krynn. Not charted on this map yet.

sources.title: Concordance of Arcane Space (cited by the Forgotten Realms Wiki)

spheres.name: Herospace
spheres.summary: A sphere with nine small suns of different colors, each with a single planet. Each planet holds the people of one alignment. Twenty mages, the Rational Order of Magistrates, control the sphere and let only exceptional people settle there.
facts: The Rational Order of Magistrates, from the moon Borden

spheres.name: Greatspace
spheres.summary: An advanced sphere whose people trust science more than magic. House Shambrath of the planet Thesalys governs it, and its people honor the Olympian gods.

spheres.name: Darkspace
spheres.summary: A dead sphere around the cold husk of a dark sun. Debris as large as moons fills it, and the vampire T'Laan rules it.

spheres.name: Faeriespace
spheres.summary: A magical sphere that one enormous tree fills, lit by sixteen suns. All its peoples live in peace as one community.

spheres.name: Clusterspace
spheres.summary: An ancient, isolated sphere with no planets: it holds planetoids, asteroid belts and built habitats. Ships enter it easily but cannot break out from inside, and only living ships leave freely. Some sages think that mind flayers began here.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

spheres.name: Refuge
spheres.summary: A small sphere near Realmspace that the Arcane control. It is a way station where spacefarers find aid and supplies, and it takes its name from its moon, Refuge.

spheres.name: Pirtelspace
spheres.summary: A cold, thinly settled sphere named for the explorer Anthonius Pirtel, the Ice Mage. It drifted into the Arcane Inner Flow and stayed there. A cool red star lights two worlds, an asteroid belt and an asteroid shell.

spheres.name: Darnannonspace
spheres.summary: A sphere of the Arcane Inner Flow that elves control. Pirtelspace lies halfway between it and Refuge.

spheres.name: Vodonispace
spheres.summary: The home sphere of the Vodoni Empire. Emperor Vulkaran the Dark rules twelve spheres from the Imperial Palace on the planet Vulkarus.

spheres.name: Golotspace
spheres.summary: Dragons rule the skies of the planet Golot, and its humans are an oppressed underclass. The Vodoni Empire holds the sphere.

spheres.name: Gorthspace
spheres.summary: A sphere at the center of the Vodoni Empire. Its one habitable planet, Gorth, is ancient forest with animals but no people, and Vodoni soldiers hunt there on leave.

spheres.name: Kofuspace
spheres.summary: A solid sphere: black shell material fills it to the core. Its worlds are air bubbles in the rock, each with a small sun, and the Kofu, peaceful dark-skinned elves, farm them.

spheres.name: Kra'akenspace
spheres.summary: A sphere full of breathable air, with no planets. Large green asteroids of porous organic material float in it, and the winged Kra'aken live in floating biospheres.

spheres.name: Lostspace
spheres.summary: A burned-out sphere, wrecked by war and not by nature. Weapons and the remains of ships and cities are everywhere, and nobody knows what happened to its people.

spheres.name: Passarspace
spheres.summary: A sphere with no sun and no native life, full of asteroids and planetoids. The Vodoni mine it and keep battle stations here.

spheres.name: Salzarspace
spheres.summary: One small water world at the center, with eight fiery stars that roll around the inside of the shell. When two stars meet, they pass through each other in an explosion. The Salzarians are living balls of water 500 feet across.

spheres.name: Thasiaspace
spheres.summary: A huge jungle planet, Thasia, around the star Lifegiver. Its people resisted the Vodoni invasion far better than the Emperor expected.

spheres.name: Vergonspace
spheres.summary: Six inhabited planets that have fought one another for centuries. The Vodoni supply weapons to all sides to keep them weak.

spheres.name: Vodonikaspace
spheres.summary: The sphere nearest to Vodonispace. The Vodoni settled all five of its planets after they destroyed the people who lived there. Its name means "New Vodoni".

spheres.name: Zalanispace
spheres.summary: The Zalani look fearsome, but they prefer art and talk. When Vulkaran learned this, he conquered them.

spheres.name: Glowrings Sphere
spheres.summary: A sphere that the scro invaded in the Second Unhuman War.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Maelstrom's Eye

spheres.name: Heartspace
spheres.summary: A busy sphere famous for the Great Archive, a store of knowledge on the planet Crescent. Its bloated red sun, the Heart, seems to beat like a living heart.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

spheres.name: Herdspace
spheres.summary: A hollow world: the inside of the shell has gravity, air, lakes, forests and grasslands, and huge beasts graze there.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Maelstrom's Eye

spheres.name: Nexspace
spheres.summary: A small, forbidden sphere, approximately 100 million miles across, home of the half-legendary planet Nex and of an ancient race that can reshape worlds. Few who search for it return.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

spheres.name: Ouiyan Reborn
spheres.summary: A sphere that the Spelljammer and Teldin Moore made in honor of Ouiyan. Some of its worlds carry the names of Ouiyan's worlds.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Ultimate Helm

spheres.name: Pathspace
spheres.summary: Little is known of this sphere, except that the planet Devis is in it.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: Into the Void
The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

spheres.name: Primespace
spheres.summary: A distant sphere. A trading outpost at its edge deals with anyone, even a mind flayer ship, and asks no questions.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

spheres.name: Vistaspace
spheres.summary: Home of Garrash, a dull-red fire world with a ring of liquid fire, under a small blue-white sun. Its currents lead to Primespace and to the Pearls, a group of six spheres.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

spheres.name: Wayspace
spheres.summary: Home of Waypoint, a desert world. Little else is known.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: Into the Void

spheres.name: Winterspace
spheres.summary: A busy trade sphere that the Elven Imperial Navy controls. After the First Unhuman War, the elves imprisoned the last of the goblin fleet here. An hourglass of stars sits at its center.
facts: About 45 days, by small fast currents

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Radiant Dragon

spheres.name: Steel Star
spheres.summary: A remote, half-legendary sphere named for its dull gray fire world. Ogres who survived the First Unhuman War rebuild their fleet here around their last kingship. Khelben Arunsun of Toril confirmed that it exists.

spheres.name: Redeyes
spheres.summary: A huge sphere with two large dark-red fire bodies. It lies between human and mind flayer space, so it is often a battleground, and wreckage fills it. A death tyrant and many scavvers live here.

spheres.name: Moragspace
spheres.summary: A small sphere that centuries of war broke: its planets are fragments, and few natives remain. The scro rule it from Gamaro Base.

spheres.name: Shadowspace
spheres.summary: A small, little-known sphere full of black fog. You can see planets only from within 20,000 miles.

spheres.name: The Dead Shell
spheres.summary: A cold, dark sphere whose primary is a black hole a few miles across, ringed by reddish gas. The Juna, an ancient precursor race, possibly lived here.

spheres.name: Chronos
spheres.summary: A sphere at war for more than 300 years. When too few mages remained to helm the fleets, its mages made a new way to power spelljamming ships.

spheres.name: Homespace
spheres.summary: The home sphere of Chila Irontooth of the Land of Kasros. Little else is known.

sources.title: The Legend of Spelljammer: Captains and Ships

spheres.name: Theiaspace
spheres.summary: The home sphere of the Pandros Line, a successful shipping line of whaleships that the halfling Calia Thornbow runs.

sources.title: The Legend of Spelljammer: Captains and Ships

spheres.name: Korvspace
spheres.summary: The sphere of the Korvadan Empire, a mostly elven empire that has governed the inner system from the planet Korvada for 200 years.

spheres.name: Tuhgri
spheres.summary: A little-known sphere. In 1368 DR, Lathander and Chauntea watched a new universe begin just outside it, as two tiny spheres.

spheres.name: Athasspace
spheres.summary: The sphere of Athas, the world of the Dark Sun setting. It lies in a distant part of the phlogiston, far from the Known Spheres, and the people of Athas know little of spelljamming.

sources.title: Defilers and Preservers: The Wizards of Athas
Dark Sun Campaign Setting, Revised: The Wanderer's Chronicle

spheres.name: Mystaraspace
spheres.summary: The sphere of Mystara, the world of the Mystara (Known World) setting. Spacefarers know little of it, but planar travelers know it well.

spheres.name: Aebrynisspace
spheres.summary: The sphere of Aebrynis, the world of the Birthright setting. Spacefarers think of it as a backwater.

spheres.name: Pyrespace
spheres.summary: The system of the Pyre, the setting of Spelljammer: Shadow of the Spider Moon. Five planets orbit the Pyre.

sources.title: Polyhedron #151, "Spelljammer: Shadow of the Spider Moon"

spheres.name: Doomspace
spheres.summary: A system whose jealous gods came back. They broke its crystal sphere and collapsed its sun into a black vortex, the Eye of Doom, which pulls in all that is left.
facts: The Eye of Doom, a black vortex

sources.title: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, Light of Xaryxis

spheres.name: Xaryxispace
spheres.summary: The home system of the Xaryxian Empire of astral elves: the star Xaryxis, three planets and the Imperial Citadel.

sources.title: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, Light of Xaryxis

spheres.name: Remichispace
spheres.summary: A large system named for the planet Remichi. It played a major part in the war against the Xaryxian Empire, and it has at least four planets and an asteroid belt, Basalt's Belt.

flows.summary: A strong current between Realmspace and Greyspace makes travel fast and simple in both directions.

sources.title: Concordance of Arcane Space (cited by the Forgotten Realms Wiki)

flows.summary: A one-way current from Greyspace to Krynnspace. The fastest way from Realmspace to Krynnspace goes through Greyspace.
